  • Status IDs as numbers, names only in the browser: the history and the API would need a join for every word. Rejected; the key is short text, as today.

Enforced by

TEST-WORKFLOWS (new in M4 WP-04: every rule, on both databases), ARCH-EVENTS (every change of a workflow), ARCH-VERSIONED (the editor saves with a version), SEC-MATRIX (rows for the workflow routes), and review (one judge, no second lookup).

Amendments (M4 WP-04)

What the first build of the server settled, so the later packages (WP-07 for the screens) can rely on it.

  1. No rows, no copy. The tables are created empty by the migration. Where no place uses a stored workflow, the built-in Simple counts, so an upgraded database keeps every status and no issue moves. A new organization (no issues and no workflow at the first start) gets the three starter workflows and their uses: Bug for Bug, Development for Feature, Simple for all other types.
  2. Statuses are unique by name in a workflow. A new status gets a key made from its name; a status change in a draft names a status by its key or by the name of a new one.
  3. The judge (bb_core::workflow::judge) answers allowed, needs these fields or not allowed with one of four reasons: no such change, not for you, only if, cannot fill. Each reason has its own error code. No rule is skipped by changing the type or the project: when a request changes either and the current status exists in the workflow that counts afterwards, a status change in the same request is judged in that workflow from the current status, with all its rules. When the current status does not exist there, the issue starts again in the starting status of that workflow, which is set when the request names no status, and any other status is refused. An issue that comes back from the trash, or whose project moves to another workflow, and whose workflow lacks its status starts again in the starting status, with history, inside that change. An issue that is outside its workflow in any other way may go only to the starting status; there is no free move. The one exception is the move of Publish for the issues of a dropped status, which the publisher sends where they chose (amendment 11). A rule that names a field the person may not see turns the change down as cannot fill without naming it, before any value is looked at. Needs is the empty Must be filled in fields and the Ask for fields the request does not carry.
  4. Who may change a workflow. The permission Manage workflows is checked at the place of the workflow: the project that contains all of its uses, or the organization. It is never held through an access key.
  5. No change to workflows strands an issue. One check, "every live issue that is governed after the change has a status of its workflow", runs on the places and workflows as they will be, inside the transaction of the change; Publish, a place that uses another workflow (or follows its parent again) and taking a workflow away all call it, and refuse with workflow.status-in-use when it fails. Publish judges every move of an issue of a dropped status first, with the rights of the person who publishes and as amendment 11 says; if any issue could not be moved, or there are more issues than amendment 12 allows, nothing is published. The moves are made inside the same change, each with its history, so nothing is answered as an error after the workflow was saved. The places the check looks at are read in the transaction, after the lock; Publish, switching a place, taking a workflow away, a change of where a type or a group is offered (ADR-0027) and retiring an issue type take the lock of the workflows alone, which waits for every holder of the shared one. Creating, changing and moving an issue, and putting a label on one, take it shared (lock_chain_in), before the lock on the codes of the project, and look at the workflow and the offers again, refusing with edit.version-changed if the status is gone. The one order of all locks is LockClass in bb-store and is kept by a guard in every transaction (ARCH-LOCK-ORDER). Issues in the trash keep their status; on restore amendment 3 applies. The issues to look at are found in SQL by the projects, types and statuses concerned, with indexes on project and status and on type and status, a page at a time (amendment 12).
  6. Which roles may change a field here (M3-F53) is one question of the policy (bb_policy::roles_that_change); the route getWhoMayChange answers it for the sentence of a refusal and for Who can do it. It names only roles somebody holds in the project, answers not found for a field the reader may not see, and names no role to a reader who is not shown the people of the project by role.
  7. Statement budget. The workflows that count are read once for a request: two statements when places use stored workflows (the uses come with the statuses), one when none does. The ceiling of the reads of an issue page (PERF-05) went from 45 to 46 for them, and to 47 with the step that reads the files of the issue (M4 WP-05; perf_queries.rs).
  8. A workflow's place never moves. A place may use only a workflow that sits at that place or above it (the lowest project that holds all its uses, or the organization), and a workflow used nowhere is the organization's to hand out. The list of workflows for a place holds only those.
  9. Nothing of a hidden field or group leaks through the editor. Publish refuses a new or changed rule that names a field the publisher may not see at the place or a group they may not know; rules that are there stay as they are. Try it answers cannot fill, with no field and no detail, for a change whose rules name a field the person who tries cannot see.
  10. Where a workflow sits can move down, never up. The place of a workflow is the lowest project that holds all its uses. When the use at its top is taken away, the place moves down to the next one; no use can be added above it, because a place may use only a workflow at or above it (amendment 8). So a person who could manage it before can still manage it after.

Amendments (M4 WP-07)

  1. Where the issues of a dropped status go. Publish asks, for each dropped status that issues are in, which status of the new workflow they go to; any status of the new workflow is allowed, not only the starting status (M4-F42). The move is not a status change: it is judged with the rights of the person who publishes (they see the issue, may change it, and their level for Status is Can change) and with no rule of a status change (Who can do it, Only if …, Must be filled in, Ask for). It is made inside the same change as the publish, under the workflows lock and before the check of amendment 5, each move with its history and with the closed date following the group of the target. A move names its target by its key, or, for a status that is new in the draft, by its name, like a status change does (amendment 2); the server resolves it. If any issue is one the publisher cannot move, nothing is published. The rights are judged when the moves are planned, in the same way as in the other use cases, not again inside the transaction.
  2. What Publish tells before it asks. The route previewPublishWorkflow (needs Manage workflows at the place where the workflow sits: the lowest project that all its uses sit in or below, which holds the permission at every place the workflow is used; the organization when it is used there, nowhere, or by projects that share no project, and then the permission for the whole organization; changes nothing, takes no lock) judges the workflow the editor would send with the code of Publish itself and answers the dropped statuses, and for each: how many live issues are in it, a few of them named as a list shows an issue, how many the person does not see, and how many the person could not move (M4-F43). Issues the person does not see are counted and never named or described. It also answers the most issues one publish moves (MANY_CHANGES_ISSUES_MAX); a publish that would move more is refused and the editor says so in plain words. The issues are read a page at a time and the reading stops one past MANY_CHANGES_ISSUES_MAX: a publish that would move more is refused with workflow.status-in-use, and the preview then says too_many and neither judges nor names issues. A job for a larger move is not built (M4-F45, decided with the lead: wait until an organization reaches the limit).
  3. Many issues carry the words of the status change. Change many issues sends the status change that was chosen, its status and the words of its button. An issue is changed only when its own workflow has exactly that change from the status the issue is in, and is skipped with the reason workflow otherwise, also when its workflow has another change to the same status with other words. The list of the status changes of a project (getProjectStatuses) is the list of the choices, each status and words once.
  4. The description is never asked for. A rule may require the description to be filled in, but not ask for it in the small form of a status change: it is long text with a lock of its own that a change cannot carry. bb_core::workflow::ask_may_name says so once; Publish refuses such a rule as workflow.invalid, and the editor offers Ask for only the fields the server marks as askable. A need for the description reaches the issue as the kind description, which the browser answers with a note to write it first.

ADR-0032: Files: stored by content, checked from their content, previews in a separate process

Status: Accepted · 2026-10-16 · refines ATT-01…ATT-04, ATT-07, SEC-13; owner's answers M4-Q3, M4-Q4

Context

M4 lets people add files to issues and comments (ATT-01). A file is the most dangerous thing a person can give the server. It may claim to be an image and be a script, it may be an SVG or HTML page that runs in the browser, it may be a small file that unpacks to gigabytes, and it may be built to crash the program that reads it. The data folder already has an empty files/ folder (architecture §6), and bb-files is an empty crate.

Decision

1. Storage
  • A file is stored once, by the SHA-256 of its content, under files/ in the data folder, outside any web root (ATT-02). The server never serves that folder directly.
  • An attachment points to a file and to its issue or comment. It records who added it, its name and its real type.
  • A file is deleted when no attachment, document version or keep rule points to it any more. A daily job (ADR-0017) does it. Enforced by: a test of the job on both databases (M4 WP-05).
  • A deleted attachment goes to the trash with Undo, like an issue (M4-Q3).
  • Storage sits behind a port (FileStore in bb-app), so S3-compatible storage (ATT-06, V1) is a second adapter later. Enforced by: ARCH-DEPS (bb-app never imports bb-files).
2. Uploads
  • Parts: an upload goes in parts. Bugaboo's own small protocol: start an upload (size, name), send parts with their offset, finish. An interrupted upload goes on from the last part the server has. An unfinished upload is deleted after a day. No extra library.
  • Body limit: each upload route sets its own body limit for a part. All other routes keep the 1 MiB limit (M1-F30).
  • Size (M4-Q4): at most 25 MiB per file by default. A project may set less, and the organization up to 100 MiB (a MiB is 1,048,576 bytes; the settings count in these units). A file over the limit is refused before its parts are stored.
  • Type: the real type is read from the content (infer), never trusted from the name or the browser (ATT-03). All types are accepted. The organization may list types it never accepts (for example .exe).
  • Who may add: a person who may change the issue (Guests on the issues they reported), or a person who may comment, for files on their own comment (M4-Q3).
  • Who may delete: whoever may change issues, and the person who added the file while they may still add one there (the rule of comments: the right to change the issue for a file of the issue, the right to comment for a file of a comment). Undo follows the same rule.
  • Enforced by: TEST-UPLOADS (new in M4 WP-05) and SEC-MATRIX.
3. Downloads
  • Signed links: a download goes through a signed link, valid for 5 minutes and for one person (ATT-07).
  • Checked every time: every download checks again that the person still sees the issue and the comment, so a link a person passes on, or keeps after losing access, stops working. Enforced by: TEST-UPLOADS and SEC-MATRIX.
  • Headers: every download is sent with Content-Disposition: attachment, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and the content security policy default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; sandbox, which allows nothing and lets no page frame it. Enforced by: SEC-HEADERS (the policy is exactly that, and no other code sets the policy header).
  • No HTML or SVG in the page: SVG, HTML and every other type the browser could run are never shown inside Bugaboo, only downloaded.
4. Previews
  • Images and PDFs get a preview: a small image the server makes (ATT-04). Nothing else does.
  • In a separate process: a preview is made by bugaboo preview, a child process with limits on memory, time and pixels (a named constant each). It is given nothing of the server's: an empty environment, the previews work folder as its working folder and the bytes of the file on its standard input (no path); it writes one small PNG on its standard output. That is not a sandbox: the child runs as the account of the server and so holds that account's rights (if code runs in it, it can read the keys and the database and reach the network). The protection is the separation of the process, the limits on memory, time and pixels, and the small set of decoders; it stops crashes and bombs, not a compromise through a memory-safety bug in a decoder. Hardening (landlock or seccomp on Linux, a separate user, a restricted token on Windows) is the follow-up M4-F121, and the risk is among the accepted risks of the security architecture. A file that is too big, takes too long or crashes the child gets no preview, and the server goes on.
  • As a job: previews are made in a job (ADR-0017), at most a few at once (the worker pool of ADR-0017).
  • Libraries: image for images and hayro for PDFs, both pure Rust. hayro's license is checked before it is added (DEP-LICENSES).
  • Served like files: a preview is shown in the page as an image from our own origin, through a signed link like the file itself.
  • Enforced by: TEST-UPLOADS (a decompression bomb, a broken PDF and a huge image each end with no preview and a running server).
5. Personal data
  • An attachment records who added it, and a file's content is personal data like a comment.
  • Files of an issue in the trash are kept as long as the issue is. Nothing purges trashed issues yet, so the files of a deleted issue are kept until the purge of the trash exists (M9, with the deletion rules for personal data; M4-F131). Trashed attachments of a live issue go after 30 days (files.clean-up).
  • Enforced by: DATA-MARKS.

Consequences

  • The issue page gets a Files block. Comments show their files. The many-issues bar does not add files.
  • Virus scanning (ATT-05) stays V1: the port has room for a scan step before a file becomes visible.

Alternatives considered

  • tus or another upload library: more than we need, and one more dependency in the browser and the server. Rejected for our own three routes.
  • Previews in the server process: a crafted file could take the server down. Rejected.
  • Files in the database: backups grow with every screenshot, and PostgreSQL large objects are awkward. Rejected; the database holds only the attachment rows.

Built in M4 WP-05

What the build decided where this record left a choice:

  • Protocol. The upload protocol says offset: a part names where it starts, and the server answers with the offset of its copy (no counter that grows, ARCH-NO-COUNTERS). A browser that lost the connection asks where the server stands and goes on from there; Try again goes on with the same upload, and a refusal or Close throws it away. A person who loses access in the middle of an upload ends it: the next part or the finish is refused and its bytes and row are thrown away at once.
  • Limits. A person has at most 20 open uploads that declare at most four times the biggest file together (OPEN_UPLOADS_MAX, OPEN_UPLOADS_BYTES_MAX; the count, the sum and the insert are one step); an issue holds at most 200 files, those in the trash included, judged when an upload starts and again when it finishes; a part is refused (file.no-room, 507) when the disk would be left with less than 1 GiB (DISK_KEPT_FREE_BYTES).
  • Names. A name loses the dots and spaces at its end (Windows drops them) and is refused with a control or format character in it (U+202E turns gpj.exe into exe.jpg on the screen), before the list of blocked types is read.
  • Downloads. A download is the bytes of the file, always sent as application/octet-stream; a preview is always image/png. The type found in the content is only shown to people. The key of the signed links is the key of the CSRF tokens, kept apart by a name of its own that every signature starts with (bugaboo.link.v1).
  • Previews. Every attachment has its own preview status (pending, ready or without) and its own job files.preview. A file that is stored already is not told apart from a new one: finishing it answers exactly as for a new file, with no preview and no link; the job of the attachment takes an existing preview of the same content only when it runs, as the attachment's own status, and makes none again. The page reads the list again while a preview is pending.
  • Jobs. Only the clean-up is daily (ADR-0017): files.clean-up deletes unfinished uploads after one day, trashed attachments after 30 days, and files nothing points to. A file is held (FileStore::hold) from putting its bytes into the store until its attachment is there, and the clean-up holds it while it deletes the row, by one conditional statement, and then the bytes, so it cannot take the bytes of a file that is being added.
  • The child process. It starts with an empty environment, the previews work folder as its working folder, the bytes of the file on standard input and one PNG on standard output; the server reads at most one byte more than a preview may have and writes the file itself. Before it reads a byte it limits itself: pixels (40 million, from the header), what the decoder may allocate (512 MiB), input size (the biggest file the settings allow), and memory. The memory limit is MAX_CHILD_MEMORY_BYTES (1 GiB) on the heap on every system, by the cap allocator that the program runs with (a refused allocation ends the child, and the server reads that as no preview), and on Linux also MAX_CHILD_ADDRESS_SPACE_BYTES (2 GiB) of address space by setrlimit. On Windows there is no limit of the address space: no safe crate sets the memory limit of a job object, and unsafe code is forbidden; the heap limit counts what Rust code asks for, not stacks, code or what the system maps. The server stops the child after 20 seconds. The test att_04_a_pdf_bomb_costs_the_child_its_memory_limit_and_the_preview_only runs the real program on a PDF whose picture unpacks to one and a half times the limit.
  • Accepted risk: the time of the preview (§4). The preview of a file that is stored already is taken over by the job of its attachment as soon as that job runs, while the preview of a new file is made first, which takes longer. A person who adds a picture or a PDF and watches how soon its preview appears can tell, a little, that the same content was stored before, by somebody they cannot know. The statuses and links in every answer are the same, no delay is added, and the risk is accepted: the person already holds the content, nothing of the other attachment is shown, and a delay as long as the slowest preview would make every picture wait.
  • Accepted risk. Finishing a file that is stored already is a little faster than finishing a new one (the bytes are not moved), so a person who measures the time can tell that the same content was stored before, by somebody they cannot know. Nothing else tells it: the answers are the same. Recorded in the security chapter, accepted because the content is already known to the person who adds it, nothing of the other attachment is shown, and equal time would mean reading and writing the file again for nothing.

Enforced by

TEST-UPLOADS (new), SEC-MATRIX (attachment routes and downloads), SEC-HEADERS (download headers), ARCH-DEPS (the port), DATA-MARKS, DEP-LICENSES and DEP-REGISTER (infer, image, hayro), and review (no route serves files/ directly).

ADR-0033: Notifications and e-mail: an outbox reader that checks again before it tells anyone

Status: Accepted · 2026-10-16 · refines NTF-01, NTF-02, SEC-06, SEC-16, PRIV-05, PRIV-08, PRIV-12 and ADR-0007; decisions M4-Q5…Q7, M4-Q9, M4-Q10

Context

Since M3, Bugaboo stores who follows an issue, who is mentioned, and the notes of Ask … to finish and Edit anyway, but it tells nobody (M3-Q3, M3-F75). M4 adds notifications in the app (NTF-01) and by e-mail (NTF-02). A notification is a copy of information sent to one person, and an e-mail leaves the server, so both must show only what that person may see at the moment they see it (SEC-06, PRIV-12, ADR-0004). bb-notify is an empty crate, and the outbox has one reader, history (ADR-0007).

Decision

1. An outbox reader builds notifications

  • A second outbox reader, notifications, turns events into notification rows, one for each person who should hear about them. Like history, it is idempotent, keeps its place, and resumes after a restart (ADR-0007).

  • Who hears about what (the defaults of M4-Q5; each person changes them under Customize):

    EventIn the appBy e-mail
    You are mentionedonon
    You are assignedonon
    A status change, a comment or a file on an issue you followonoff
    Other changes to issues you followoffoff
    Your change to many issues has endedonoff
    Ask … to finish and Edit anyway on your textonoff

  • A person is never told about their own changes.

2. Checked when built and again when shown or sent
  • When the reader builds a row, it skips a person who may not see the issue, and it leaves out every field that person may not see (the reader's mask, ADR-0004). Enforced by: SEC-MATRIX.
  • When the row is shown in the app or put into an e-mail, Bugaboo checks again: a person who lost access in between gets nothing, and a follower who lost access is dropped from the followers when the reader builds the next event for the issue (M3-F132).
  • People in a notification come as PersonRef, so Who sees people holds (ADR-0022).
  • Enforced by: SEC-MATRIX (the e-mail and notifications column, M2-F65) and ARCH-PERSON-REF.
3. E-mail
  • Off at the start: e-mail stays off until an administrator enters the organization's mail server and switches it on (PRIV-08). Send me a test e-mail tries the settings. The mail password is stored encrypted like other secrets (SEC-16).
  • Sending: each e-mail is a mail.send job (ADR-0017), sent with lettre.
  • Batching: changes to one issue within 5 minutes go into one e-mail. There is no daily summary in M4 (M4-Q6).
  • Contents: the issue ID and title, who changed what, and the comment text, all filtered as in 2, with a link into Bugaboo. An e-mail is plain text only: nothing is rendered, no file is attached, no picture loads from outside. The real link comes first, before any text of a person; a comment is quoted line by line (> ), so it cannot pass for the text of Bugaboo; control characters and the characters that turn text round or hide in it (marks of direction, zero-width characters) are removed.
  • Short e-mails: an organization setting leaves out all issue text (title and comments). It is for places where mail leaves the company.
  • Addresses in logs: e-mail addresses never appear in logs. Enforced by: DATA-LOGS.
  • Signing up proves the address (M1-F38, M4-Q10): signing up on one's own is a self-invitation. The person gives only an address; nothing is made until they open the link sent to it (valid for 24 hours, used once). The link opens the invitation page, where they choose a name and a password and the account is made. The answer is the same for every address, and an address that has an account gets an e-mail that says so. Signing up needs e-mail.
4. In the app
  • Notifications is a page and a menu entry with the number of unread ones (UX §4.11).
    • Entries are grouped by issue, newest first.
    • Each entry has Open, which goes to the exact comment or change, and Mark as read.
  • Notifications replaces the Mentions block on the start page. Mentions becomes a filter, and the start page shows the newest unread ones (M4-Q7).
5. Keeping and deleting
  • Notifications are deleted after 90 days (PRIV-05, UX §5.7). A sent e-mail's job and its payload go when it is sent, or when it dies, with the dead jobs' keep period (M1-F21).
  • Enforced by: DATA-MARKS and the keep-and-delete job's test.
6. Handles for mentions (M3-F70, M4-Q9)
  • Every person gets a short handle (@ana.brandt), made from the name when the account is made, unique, and changeable in My settings.
  • A mention stores the person, not the handle, so a changed handle never breaks an old comment.
  • A handle is people information and follows Who sees people.
  • A handle has only the ASCII letters a…z, digits, ., - and _. A name is spelled with them (ä is ae); a name with none of them gets the handle person.
  • A new text resolves only the handle a person has now. The handle they gave up stays reserved, so nobody else can take it, and the texts written before keep naming them because a mention stores the person.
  • A person cannot have the handle of a group or a role, and a group or a role cannot be given a name whose handle a person has or had, so an @handle never names two things. A person changes their handle once in seven days; the handle they were given with the account does not count.

Consequences

  • bb-notify holds the e-mail adapter behind a port (Mailer in bb-app). Tests use a fake mailer that keeps what it would have sent.
  • Webhooks (NTF-03) and live updates later read the same outbox the same way.

Alternatives considered

  • Sending from the use case that made the change: the change would wait for the mail server, and a failed mail could undo nothing. Rejected; ADR-0007 already gives the outbox.
  • Filtering only when the row is built: a person who loses access an hour later would still read yesterday's notifications. Rejected; checking again costs one permission lookup per row shown.

Amendment (M4 WP-06)

The reader and the e-mail are built. What the build decided where this record left room:

  • The reader. notifications is read by run_due_jobs before the jobs are taken, in batches of 200 events. A row is unique by the recipient and what it is about (once: the event, or the mention), so a restart that repeats a batch makes no second row. The rows, the jobs they queue and the new place of the reader are one transaction.
  • Followers. A follower hears only of events from the time they began to follow. A follower who lost access is dropped when the reader builds the next event for the issue.
  • Shaped when shown. A row keeps the changes and the person who made them. Every time it is listed or put in an e-mail it is shaped again for the recipient: the fields they may see, the people as Who sees people says (the same words as the history of an issue), the issue only if they still see it. The number of unread notifications is a route of its own, capped, and counts only rows that still show. One request for the list looks at a bounded number of rows and answers with a cursor when there are more.
  • E-mail. Plain text only. One mail.send job for each person and issue is queued for 5 minutes after the first change; it takes every waiting row of that pair, and when more wait than the e-mail holds it says so and marks all of them, so a second e-mail does not repeat the first. A failed job is tried again with the pause of the job runner and the rows stay waiting; when it gives up, the rows are marked as never sent.
  • The mail server. The password has its own routes (PUT /api/v1/mail/password, Send me a test e-mail). The test e-mail is sent at once, not as a job, and a person sends one every 10 seconds at most. Settings that would send a user name or a password without encryption to a mail server on another machine are refused (mail.insecure). Only the certificate authorities built into Bugaboo are trusted.
  • Signing up. Signing up is a self-invitation (§3): sign_up takes an address, answers 202 with check_your_mail for every address, and queues a mail.send job; the job makes the SignUpInvitation (its own table, read as an invitation with nobody who invited) and sends the link, or, for an address that has an account, an e-mail that says so. A second sign-up for the same address within 10 minutes sends nothing. sign_up is refused while e-mail is off, and the status answer sign_up_open says so. sessions.purge deletes the links that were used or ran out.
  • Keeping. Five more kinds of job: notifications.purge (rows after 90 days, and the payload of dead jobs after 30), security-log.prune (the setting Days to keep the security log, 365 at the start), sessions.purge, server-log.rotate (the size and the number of files are settings) and mail.send. Each can run twice with the same result.
  • Tags. Renaming or combining tags counts each touched issue's version in the same change that rewrites its tags (M3-F126); a rename of a very large tag is therefore one long change, which a step job could split later.
  • Delivery in the matrix. The record of SEC-MATRIX has a delivery line for each entry point (notifications, e-mail) and each starting role as the recipient; the check compares it with the tables of the starting roles.

Amendment (M4 WP-08)

The screens are built. What the build decided where this record left room:

  • The count. The number on the menu entry and on the bar of a phone is GET /api/v1/notifications/unread. Until live updates arrive the browser asks every 30 seconds (the time of the check of versions, ADR-0019) and when the person comes back to the tab. A count of AT_ONCE_MAX is shown as 100+.
  • Open. Open goes to the issue with ?comment=<ID> for a comment and ?change=<moment> for a change. The issue page marks the entry and reads earlier pages of the history until it finds it. A change is found by the moment it happened, to the millisecond, because the history and a notification are made from the same event.
  • The text of a comment in a notification is HTML that the server made with bb-markdown for this reader (the mark x-safe-html on NotificationEntry.html), so the browser draws it as it draws a comment.
  • Customize is My settings › Notification settings. Its rows come from NotificationKind::setting: cargo xtask gen api reads that function and writes the table into the browser client, so the settings of a kind are written once.
  • The mail server is Organization settings › Connections › E-mail & notifications. The settings are the registry's (mail.*); the password goes through PUT /api/v1/mail/password and is never read back. GET /api/v1/mail says whether one is set (credential_set) and the server's own judgement of the mail server as entered (readiness: ready, incomplete when the host or the sender is missing, or insecure when a secret would go without encryption to another machine). It comes from the same code the test e-mail and the jobs use (mail_server), so the page shows the judgement and holds no copy of the rule. credential_set is a yes or no and not a secret: it tells an administrator who may change the mail server nothing they could not see by trying the test e-mail, and the page needs it to show not set. A change of the mail server, its port or the user name deletes the stored password in the same change (the event records it), so a new server is never handed the old password; the page then shows not set. The refusals of Send me a test e-mail are shown in words: not entered (mail.off), a user name or password in the clear to another machine (mail.insecure), turned away (mail.rejected, status 502), not reached (mail.unavailable), and too soon (rate-limit.exceeded, once in 10 seconds for a person; the button waits that long too).
  • The wait for the changes of one e-mail is the start-up setting mail_batch_seconds (BUGABOO_MAIL_BATCH_SECONDS, 300 unless set), so a test or a demo can see the e-mail in seconds.
  • The first start has an optional step for the mail server after the second check of the account.
  • Signing up shows Check your e-mail after the form. Asking for a new link waits as long as the server does for one address (RESEND_AFTER_MINUTES), and the route has its own limit; a link that ran out leads to asking for a new one. While e-mail is off, the switch for signing up says so.
  • The Mentions block of the start page is gone. The routes /api/v1/me/mentions and /api/v1/me/mentions/read are removed: there is one way to read mentions, the notifications.

Amendment (M4 WP-13): one wording for the screen and the e-mail

The words of a change and of a notification are chosen once, in bb-core (wording). The server's e-mails call the code directly and the browser calls the same code through bb-wasm (ADR-0005), from the lazy parts only: the history of an issue, the notifications, the preview of a change to many issues and the sentence about a conflict on the issue page. They load the module with import() and show a skeleton until it is there (the first page does not grow; the module has its own budget, PERF-04). The workflow editor loads one more thing the same way: the rule of the same name (bb_core::names, name_key), so that Add and Rename of a status say a name is taken by the rule of the server and not by one written again in the browser (M4 WP-14); the editor keeps that check off until the module is there, and the refusal of the server stays the judge.

  • What is shared. The choice of sentence (changed, set, cleared, the long text), the message keys and the sentences of every kind of notification, the words of a status and a priority, yes and no, a length of time, a list of names, and the rule that a line of an e-mail gets no full stop after a value that ends in ., ? or !. The result is a tree of message keys and values (Said); it holds no English. The server renders it with its catalog, the browser looks the keys up in its own.
  • What is not shared, with the owner's approval. Approved by the owner on 2026-10-22: region-dependent formatting of dates, numbers and time zones is kept in two implementations, because the browser's device choice uses Intl, which the server cannot run. They are held together by vectors generated from Rust: cargo xtask gen word-vectors writes tools/testdata/value-words.json from bb_core::wording::vectors (the expected words are what the server writes), DOC-GENERATED fails when the file differs from that code, and the browser test web/app/src/shared/value-words.test.ts fails when the screen writes a case differently. The cases hold half-up rounding, the 12-hour clock, and the fixed date orders (day first, month first, year first).
  • The same vectors hold the small helpers of the screens that cannot wait for the module. The field on the issue page (ownValueText, durationText) and the lists of names all over the app (listText) are written synchronously and are not part of a history or a notification. Their yes and no, length of time and list words are checked against the vectors generated from Rust, so a difference from the shared code fails the browser test. This is part of the same approval.
  • The types of the input and the output of the module are generated from the Rust structs (cargo xtask gen word-types writes web/packages/wasm/src/wording.generated.ts, DOC-GENERATED holds it), and the module refuses an input it cannot read with an error that the app throws in development and under test, so a mismatch is found at once and not shown as empty words.
  • The input of the module is built by each side from its own data (the API items of the browser, the shaped notifications of the server): the names of people, the name of a field and, for a number, a day or a moment, the words of the region. Mapping a data shape to that input is not wording.

Enforced by

SEC-MATRIX (the e-mail and notifications column), DOC-GENERATED and the browser test of the vectors (the wording amendment), ARCH-PERSON-REF, ARCH-EVENTS, DATA-MARKS, DATA-LOGS, DEP-REGISTER (lettre), the permission tests of M4 WP-06, and review (no other path sends mail).

ADR-0034: Saved searches: owned by one person, shared without giving anyone more

Status: Accepted · 2026-10-25 · refines QRY-06, CFG-02, SEC-06, PRIV-13 and ADR-0005; decisions M5-Q1, M5-Q2, M5-Q8, M5-Q12

Context

M5 lets people save a search with how its results are shown, and share it with groups or projects (QRY-06, CFG-02). A shared search is a piece of text written by one person and read by others. It must never let a receiver see an issue, a field, a value or a person that their own rights hide, and its text must not tell them that something hidden exists.

Decision

  1. What a saved search is: a name, the canonical search text (ADR-0005, amendment M5), how it is shown (the kind of view, columns with their order and widths, Spacing, grouping), the person who made it, and the groups and projects it is shared with. It has a stable address, /s/<id>. M5 shows the kind list; board, timeline and calendar read the same record when their milestones come (M5-Q12).
  2. Private when it is made. Sharing it needs the new permission Share searches (counts per project; Administrator, Project lead, Team member, Contributor and Viewer start with it, Guest does not):
    • with a project: Share searches in that project;
    • with a group: Share searches for the whole organization and being in that group, or Manage groups. The Share window lists only the groups and projects the person may share with (UX design §4.3).
  3. It always runs with the rights of the person who opens it (QRY-05). Two people may see different issues in the same search, and being shared with never adds rights.
  4. A receiver sees a shared search only when its text checks cleanly against their own rights: every field it names is one they may read, and every person, group and project it names is one they may see. Otherwise it is not listed for them, and its address answers exactly like an address that does not exist. Its name and text never reach them.
  5. Only the person who made it changes, shares or deletes it. A person with Change organization settings may delete any saved search. Everyone who sees it may Save a copy, which is private and their own.
  6. A project's default list (M5-Q2): a person with Change project settings may choose a saved search shared with the project as the project's default list. Without one, the project shows the built-in default: the columns of UX design §4.2 (status, ID, type, title, labels, priority, assigned, changed), grouped by status, Comfortable. A project's list and the Search page are the same screen; the project's list is the search with within KEY filled in (M5-Q8).
  7. Changes are events (ADR-0007): made, changed, shared, no longer shared, deleted. Deleting goes to the trash with Undo, like issues.
  8. Personal data: the name and the text are content written by a person (marked as such). When the person who made a search is removed, their private searches go with them; a shared search stays, made by Former user …, and a person with Change organization settings may delete it.

Consequences

  • The checker of the search language runs twice for a shared search: once for the person who saves it, and once for each receiver when it is listed or opened. It is pure and fast, so this costs little.
  • A receiver whose rights shrink loses the search from their list without a message.
  • Saved searches are the base of later features: standing rules for agents (ADR-0029), dashboards and e-mailed searches (QRY-07, V1).

Alternatives considered

  • Shared searches run with the rights of the person who made them: a receiver would see what only the maker may see. Rejected (SEC-06).
  • Show a shared search with a hidden field as "This search uses something you cannot see": it tells the receiver that the field exists, which is what an unknown field must never tell (QRY-05). Rejected.
  • Anyone may edit a shared search: a search changes under the people who rely on it. Rejected; Save a copy covers the need.

Amendment M5 WP-06 (2026-10-26): how it is stored and served

The builder of M5 WP-06 decided the following where the decision above left room:

  1. Tables (migration 23): saved_search, its columns saved_search_column (the search word of each field, its place and its width), its shares saved_search_share (a group or a project, told apart by kind; no reference for the target, so deleting a group takes its rows with it in the same change) and project_default_list (one row for each project). The maker has no reference to the person (a removed person leaves a tombstone, PRIV-04).
  2. Spacing is a choice of the setting Spacing (appearance.spacing): the registry holds its two words once and a saved search stores one of them. The widths are whole numbers in the units of the list; a list holds at most 40 columns and a saved search is shared with at most 100 places.
  3. A saved search is the person's own data: only a session reaches the routes, never an access key (ADR-0025, decision 8).
  4. Who is reached: a share with a group reaches the people in it, a share with a project the people who see it. The list Shared with me holds the searches of other people that a share reaches, oldest first, and the person's own are in the list Mine. A search that is not the person's and does not reach them, or does not check cleanly for them (item 8), is resource.not-found for every call that names it (open, copy, delete, restore, change, share), with the same reads as for an address that does not exist; one rule (Ctx::may_open) decides it for all of them. A person who reaches and reads a search, and is not its maker, is refused (access.forbidden) when they try to change, share or delete it. Taking a search out of the trash shows its name and text only to someone who may open it: a person with Change organization settings who is not the maker, and who could not open the search, is told nothing of it. A request for Shared with me looks at no more than 500 searches (bb_core::paging::LOOKED_AT_MAX, the rule of the notifications and of the projects to choose from for an access key); a page that ends there is short and has a cursor that is a count (+500) or the last search shown, never the ID of a search that was skipped; a page can also end short at the bound of the names that a request resolves (item 8), with the last search shown as its cursor.
  5. The maker is shown as the viewer sees Authors, by the rights the viewer has in the first project that reaches them (else in the organization). Whom a search is shared with is told to its maker only.
  6. The project's default list is the row of project_default_list. It is read only while the search is not in the trash, is still shared with the project and the reader may open it; stopping the share takes the row away in the same change, and choosing none takes it away too. The change is an event about the project (default_list).
  7. A person who is removed: delete_private_searches_of (the port) deletes the searches shared with nobody in the change that removes the person; the shared ones stay, and the maker's name is Former user … because the name of the person is.
  8. The check of a receiver (decision 4) is Ctx::canonical_text: the text is read and checked with the fields the person may read everywhere (Ctx::looked_in, the read that looked_at of a search has, taken from the tree and the levels read once for the request; ADR-0005 amendment M5), and the columns and the grouping must be readable fields (the Issue ID column, the word id, is the one word that is no field; it is reserved, so no own field takes it and a field named Id is refused with name.taken). Every name in the text (people, groups, member of, projects, Issue IDs, statuses, types, choices, tags, labels) is resolved by Ctx::search_names, the one function that runs a search and checks a saved one (ADR-0005 item 9): a text that names something the person cannot know (names_unknown) does not check, so a person who is shown people by their role only cannot use a saved search that names one, and an Issue ID names an issue the person reads. The same function makes the canonical text when a search is saved or changed, and a text that does not check for its maker is request.invalid. A list of shared searches skips the ones that fail and goes on within the bound of item 4, so a page that is short because searches were skipped tells nothing, but see the end of this item for one that ends at the bound of names. What resolving names reads depends on what a text names: a search that does not exist, one that does not reach the person and one that fails the check of its fields run the same reads, and only a search that a share reaches, that passes the check of its fields and fails on a name costs the reads of that name, accepted because the person could tell, by time or by a page of Shared with me that ends at the bound of names (a short page with the last search shown as its cursor, followed by an empty page), that a search shared with them exists and fails on some name, which the person who shared it chose to tell them (12-security.md, the row of saved searches; proof sec_06_a_hidden_saved_search_and_a_missing_one_run_the_same_reads). A request resolves each name once, and at most NAME_RESOLUTIONS_MAX (200) names with a read each (people and Issue IDs; the groups, tags and labels are read once as a whole). A name past the bound is never answered as unknown: the page of the list ends before that search and the next page starts after the last search shown, with a budget of its own, so every search that checks cleanly is in the list; a page with no search yet goes on to the first one it can show, at most LOOKED_AT_MAX searches looked at. The cost of a request is bounded by these two numbers; the maintainer accepted it (2026-10-27).
  9. At most 500 saved searches per person (trash included, limit.reached) and at most 100 shares of one search, counted in the change that writes, under an advisory lock of the maker (LockClass::SavedSearches) on PostgreSQL, so two requests at the same moment cannot pass the limits.

Enforced by (additional): the tests qry_06_* of bb-core, bb-app, bb-store and bb-server.

Enforced by

SEC-MATRIX (the search entry point, with saved searches), ARCH-PERMS (Share searches), ARCH-EVENTS, DATA-MARKS, PERF-N1 (the list of saved searches), and the tests of M5 WP-06 named in the security chapter.
